newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-fundamentals point to better German growth.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-fundamentals point to better German growth.

text.p: German Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that fundamental economic factors pointed to an upswing in the Germany's economic growth.

"An almost-four percent increase in capital expenditure in the last quarter of 1996, and news from engineering sector of a lively level of growth, could be the harbingers of growth in the federal republic," Welteke told journalists at a dinner.

"The fundamental conditions for growth are extremely favourable -- wage increases are moderate, because extremely high unemployment does not allow for high wage demands by unions. Also there are no indications of increased inflation."
German companies had successfully increased their productivity and introduced efficiencies and cost-saving measures, Welteke said, while attempts at reforming the tax system were under way.
Welteke, who is also president of the central bank of the state of Hesse, was speaking at a dinner organised by the International Business Journalists Forum.
